record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Optimal constants for powers of the Laplacian
record.original_question: For Lieb-Thirring inequalities for fractional or higher-order kinetic energies (−Δ)^s with s>0, determine the optimal constants L_{γ,d,s}. In particular, decide whether L_{γ,d,s} agrees with the corresponding semiclassical constant when γ is sufficiently large.

evidence.quote: While some of the above proofs yield reasonably good constants Lγ,d,s, nothing seems to be known about their optimal values for s 6= 1. In particular, one might wonder whether Lγ,d,s coincides with its semiclassical analogue for sufficiently large γ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a dimension d ≥ 1, a real exponent s > 0, and a real exponent γ ≥ 0. For a real-valued potential V on R^d with V_- := max(-V, 0) ∈ L^{γ+d/(2s)}(R^d), consider the self-adjoint Schrödinger-type operator
   H = (−Δ)^s − V(x)
on L^2(R^d), where (−Δ)^s is the fractional Laplacian defined via the Fourier multiplier |ξ|^{2s}. Let {−E_j(V)}_j denote the negative eigenvalues of H (counted with multiplicity).

A Lieb–Thirring inequality of order (γ, d, s) is a bound of the form
   Σ_j E_j(V)^γ ≤ L_{γ,d,s} ∫_{R^d} V(x)_+^{γ + d/(2s)} dx,
valid for every admissible V. Define L_{γ,d,s} as the smallest constant for which this inequality holds for all such V. The corresponding semiclassical (Weyl) constant is
   L^{sc}_{γ,d,s} := (2π)^{-d} ∫_{R^d} (|ξ|^{2s} − 1)_-^γ dξ
       = Γ(γ+1) / ( (2s)^{-1} ... )  (the explicit constant arising from the phase-space integral),
and a standard Berezin–Li–Yau type argument shows L_{γ,d,s} ≥ L^{sc}_{γ,d,s}.

Problem. Determine the value of the optimal constant L_{γ,d,s} for s ≠ 1. In particular, decide whether there exists a threshold γ_*(d, s) such that
   L_{γ,d,s} = L^{sc}_{γ,d,s}   for all γ ≥ γ_*(d, s),
and if so identify γ_*(d, s) explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: The sharp values of L_{γ,d,s} for s ≠ 1 appear to be unknown. Existing literature (e.g. Frank–Hundertmark–Jex–Nam on the semiclassical constant with gradient error term, and Hardy–Lieb–Thirring inequalities for fractional Schrödinger operators) treats non-optimal constants or strong-coupling asymptotics, and surveys describe the question of whether L_{γ,d,s} equals its semiclassical analogue for large γ as still open for s ≠ 1.

status_evidence.title: Lieb-Thirring inequality with semiclassical constant and gradient error term
status_evidence.snippet: Improved Lieb-Thirring bound with the semiclassical constant and a lower-order gradient error term, but does not establish sharpness of L_{γ,d,s} for fractional powers.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal constants for fractional kinetic energies are not known; only non-sharp bounds with the semiclassical constant plus error terms are available.

status_evidence.title: Hardy-Lieb-Thirring inequalities for fractional Schrödinger operators
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes Lieb-Thirring type bounds for (-Δ)^s minus a Hardy weight, with constants that are not claimed to be optimal.
status_evidence.claim: Constants in fractional Lieb-Thirring inequalities are generally non-optimal in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Lieb–Thirring inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses optimal constants in the classical case s=1 and notes that whether the semiclassical constant is optimal in various regimes remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality of the semiclassical constant in Lieb-Thirring bounds is a long-standing open question, including for fractional kinetic energies.
